design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 (domain_renewals_and_transfers, env_0076), revision 6. Frozen 2026-10-22 11:05:00 EDT.

[Revision 6 record] Audit revision_5 N6 (XF 13) and O19 -> every quantity that enters a credits total names itself in its own sentence as one of that total's credits ("The ... plan allowance, one of the ... credits, is ..."; the restore-day transfer price lock likewise; the price-match quantities as "one of the charge's Domain Care credits"), and each total reads "the amounts this rule names as one of the ... credits, added together" - no list of factor quantities and no positional "credits below" (superseding the revision 5 wording). Cross-product check against account_tier_benefits: the tier discount touches only the renewal component (never ICANN, restore fees or refunds), no percentage is added to or compounded with another (the bulk step is the higher-of), discounted components are rounded half up before fees, the tier read is the one on the charge date, and every seeded domain and hosting row follows the tier recorded on its charge date. Figures unchanged.

[Revision 5 record] Render scan render_r1 D1-D2 -> every credits total is defined once generically ("the credits below that apply ..., added together"), each component names "the percentage discount that applies" instead of a factor quantity, and every standard-computation sentence reads "no discount and no credit applies" (restore: "no credit and no make-good applies"; price matches: "no Domain Care credit applies to the charge, so nothing is refunded"), so the baseline is computable without naming a factor quantity (D1, XF 29); every half-up rounding adds 1e-9 dollars (1e-7 in cents) before rounding or truncating (D2, XF 28), checked against exact half-up over every renewal price, 1-10 years and tier percentages; this world's figures, baselines and sensitivities unchanged.

[Revision 4 record] Audit revision_3 N5 -> every price-difference factor is stated as the amount by which one price exceeds the other: the Business/Cloud plan allowance is never less than plan_allowance_standard per year (so a negative or zero tariff difference, e.g. .co transfer_in_price below registration_price, never lowers the credits or ranks a Business/Cloud plan below Starter), and the transfer price lock is nothing where the renewal_price does not exceed the transfer_in_price; probe t1/probe_n5.py (.co/.us/.net x Cloud 8/Starter) recorded; this world's figures unchanged; O17 phrase removed from the ladders.

[Revision 3 record] Audit revision_2 (N1-N4, T1-N1, T1-N2, T1-N4, owner ruling) -> changes: each price match's out-of-scope sentence names the three sibling price matches as set by their own rules (N1); the price match no longer prices a line: it refunds the Domain Care credits the line earns today (hosting credit, plan allowance, volume credit, autopay credit), never more than billed, so no reseller discount sits inside it (N2, T1-N1); each price match retires only the clauses governing its own line type (full amount, transfer cancellation-only bar or restore never-refunded bar, destination) (N3); the plan allowance is an honest method in every scope (Business/Cloud: TLD price less registration_price; Starter/Plus/Pro flat; none) (N4, T1-N2); the restore's credits take the autopay credit in place of a tier step (T1-N4); volume thresholds 250 / 5,000 (O9). Owner ruling (b): the restore-day extension rule states the holder pays it at checkout (PayPal or a card entered there); the persona shows the need (card on file near its limit, studio business card not on file); the user tool takes checkout_method.

[Revision 2 record, history: superseded where the revision 3 record says so] Audit r1 (C1–C9 bearing here, T1-R1..R4, T1-O1): the restore and restore-day tails now name the sibling rules and state the real base rule for every other restore/renewal (C1, C5b); the over-billing corrections became the Domain Care price match, a look-back refund of the difference between a 2022-01-01..2025-11-30 line billed under the base rules and its Domain Care price, so base "An inbound transfer is billed once at the TLD's transfer_in_price plus one icann_fee_per_year" and the restore billing rule stay true of those lines (C2); the restore's gate sentences carry the resolvers' exact scope (C3); restore-day years are the greatest whole number within the 10-year limit (C4); extension subject narrowed to domain_expiry_update so no grace or auto-renew gate is retired (C5a); no mailbox, certificate or payment-method ladder remains (C7, realism); every credit bounded so no amount reaches 0.00 (C8); payment credits, the retention count and the always-9-years term step removed from this family (C9); near-misses seeded for both price matches (cancelled Starter plan, 2024-11-12 deposit outside 12 months) (T1-R4); persona refund line made conditional (T1-O1). The customer is now a reseller web studio so the reseller dimensions bear on this world.

[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 1 -> prerequisite_problems=3, factor_counts [6,4,4,6]: redemption restore 6, restore-day extension 6, transfer-line price match 4, restore-line price match 4.
[Scope] task 1 = domain_ext_transfer_line_price_match, domain_ext_restore_line_price_match, domain_ext_redemption_restore_price, domain_ext_restore_day_extension; tools refund_transfer_in_price_match_5d5ebe85, refund_restore_price_match_9ee6604c, bill_redemption_restore_c1eb5c46, pay_restore_extension_years_823e7992 (owner=user). Disjoint from task 0; the union covers all 8 policies.

[Why a good test] The caller asks only to renew driftwoodwebworks.net for as long as allowed and to pay it. The agent must see the domain in redemption, read that restore-day years wait on an active domain with a restore dated today, that the restore fee waits on the most recent restore charge's price match and that the restore is not billed until the most recent inbound transfer charge carries its price match; price both look-back refunds as today's Domain Care credits (active Cloud 8 on a 12-month term, Business/Cloud plan allowance, deposits of the last 12 whole months, autopay with declines); price the restore with the waived fee and the late-notice make-good (post-expiry notice 8 days after expiry, ICANN ERRP schedule of 5 days); then count 9 restore-day years with the transfer price lock (transfer completed 23 whole months before) and hand the 88.18 payment over for the customer to pay at checkout with a card entered there.

[Problem-tree card] root domain_ext_restore_day_extension (user).
 RX <- RS value_input (rx_years): "Restore-day years are priced only after the domain's status reads active again and a restore charge dated the day of the order stands on it, the years being counted from the expiry date the restore leaves." Opening: status redemption. Only the restore writes that state. Skip-run 98.31 (10 years).
 RS <- CRR value_input (rs_fee): "The restore fee of a redemption restore is fixed only after the domain's most recent restore charge, where it was billed from 1 January 2022 through 30 November 2025 by card or PayPal and earns Domain Care credits, carries its price-match refund." Opening: 2025-10-27 restore 109.18 (credits 9.45), no refund. Skip-run: RS 58.23.
 RS <- CRT state_gate (negated): "A redemption restore is not billed until the domain's most recent inbound transfer charge, where it was billed from 1 January 2022 through 30 November 2025 by card or PayPal and earns Domain Care credits, carries its price-match refund." Opening: 2024-10-23 transfer 17.18 (credits 6.45), no refund.
 Order CRT, CRR, RS, RX; the price matches commute (swap identical).

[Base-invariant card] Restore: in_redemption (status redemption), redemption_window (2026-10-21 + 30 = 2026-11-20 inclusive; day 1 now; 2026-11-21 too late). Extension: active via the restore; 2036-09-20 within 10 years. Price matches: refund_once; the registration and auto-renew windows do not reach a transfer or restore line (vacuous); the transfer-cancellation-only bar (transfer line), the restore-never-refunded bar (restore line), the full-amount and destination clauses superseded for that line type's price match only and restated for every other refund.
[Business-object card] Objects: the transfer line and the 2025 restore line (refund rows carry original_domain_charge_id); the new restore and restore-day lines act on driftwoodwebworks.net only.

[Factor cards] see computations. Tiers: Bronze 3% (restore-day years only); Cloud 8 active 12 months -> hosting credit 3.00/yr; Business/Cloud plan allowance -> TLD price less registration_price (transfer 16.98 - 13.98 = 3.00; restore/renewal 19.98 - 13.98 = 6.00/yr); deposits of the last 12 whole months 971.89 -> volume 0.25/yr; auto-renew on with 2026 declines -> autopay 0.20/yr; transfer completed 23 whole months ago -> price lock once 3.00; price match standing -> restore fee waived; notice 8 days late -> make-good 1.50. Baselines: price matches 0 (no credit earned, nothing refunded), restore 109.18, restore-day extension 181.62. Near-misses: cancelled Starter plan (status filter), 2024-11-12 deposit (outside 12 months), 2025 post-expiry notice (older, before the current expiry), 2025 declines (outside 12 months).

[XF sweep]
Defining-sentence table: per-policy "<q> reseller discount / hosting credit / plan allowance / volume credit / autopay credit / transfer price lock is ..." -> the factor bindings; "The restore fee is waived ..." -> rs_fee -> restore_fee_courtesy; "The notice make-good is ..." -> rs_makegood -> restore_notice_makegood; component/amount/order/standard sentences -> plain bindings and baseline; names unique per policy (restored-year, restore-day, transfer line's, restore line's).
Factor-reads table: every factor binding reads only its own bindings, records and plain selections; assembly is plain.
Method all-pairs: plan allowance (amount by which the TLD price exceeds registration_price, never less than 0.75 per year | flat 0.75 once | none); restore fee (waived | min(fee, early fee) | fee); price lock (difference x years | once | none).
T1/T2 (restore-fee lesser-of): T1 baseline moves RS 9.23 -> 98.23; T2 the early tier gives 58.23 without a price match.
Probe table (scratch t1/probe runs): cancelled plan listed first (decoy) -> unchanged; no active plan (absent) -> hosting credit and plan allowance 0, refund falls to 0.45, no floor added; no hosting -> credits fall through; full refund on the restore line instead of a price match -> fee not waived; 2026 notice missing (2025 kept) -> missing tier 3.00; transfer completed under 12 months -> lock per year.
Events written with base triggers: restore line (card) -> domain_restore (domain); renewal line (card) -> domain_expiry_update (domain); refund lines (original_payment_method) -> no account write.
compute_basis verbatim sweep: all quotes substrings of their rules; every binding quoted; no factor id is a substring of a tool name.

[Verification] scratch t1/run.py: CRT 6.45 (base 0), CRR 9.45 (base 0), RS 9.23 (base 109.18), RX 88.18 (base 181.62); skip CRR -> RS 58.23; skip RS -> RX 98.31; skip CRT -> state gate only; swap identical.
[Draft recomputation from visible context] Redemption -> restore first; its fee waits on the restore-line price match and the restore waits on the transfer-line price match; refunds 6.45 and 9.45; restore 9.23; 10 whole months to 2027-09-20 -> 9 years -> 88.18. Agrees with gold.
[Persona] Desmond Brightwater, calm reseller web-studio owner; volunteers only the renewal goal; email + PIN on request; says go ahead to anything the agent must book; card 1286 for what the agent bills; returned money to the card only if told some is coming back; pays the long renewal himself at checkout with the studio's business card (card on file near its limit), exactly the years and amount he is given; closes on the new expiry date.
[Realism notes] Reseller tier discounts, restore fee, ICANN fee and the 5-day post-expiry notice obligation are charter figures; hosting credit, plan allowance, reseller volume credit, autopay saver, transfer price lock, early-restore and courtesy waivers and the look-back price match are Harborline's own published schedule on dimensions registrars and hosts do price on.
user_scenario:
You are Desmond Brightwater, who runs Driftwood Web Studio Inc., a two-person web studio in Toronto that resells Harborline hosting to its clients. You are calm and a bit sheepish: for a few weeks your own studio site has been showing some Harborline renewal page instead of your portfolio, you kept meaning to deal with it, and this morning a client told you your studio email bounced. You are calling to fix it now. In your words, you just want driftwoodwebworks.net renewed, and renewed for as long as Harborline is allowed to do it, because you are tired of this happening every year. You have no idea how the renewal works on Harborline's side and you never guess at prices or steps.
You give your name and the domain when the call starts. Only when the agent asks you to confirm who you are do you give the email on the account, desmond@driftwoodwebworks.net, and your support PIN, 127540; if they want one more detail, your phone number is 416-555-0127 and your billing postal code is M4L1Y7. If asked about the account, it is the studio's reseller account and you do not know the balance on it.
Whatever the agent needs to book or put right on the domain to get this done, you are fine with it: when the agent tells you about something like that, you say go ahead. Anything the agent bills for the domain itself can go on the card on file ending 1286, and if the agent tells you money is coming back to you, you ask for it to go back to the card it came from.
You want to pay for the long renewal yourself: the card on file ending 1286 is close to its limit and would not carry a renewal of many years, so when it comes to that payment you tell the agent you will pay it yourself at checkout with the studio's business card, which is not on file. When the agent tells you the number of years and the price and hands the payment over to you, you pay exactly that number of years and that amount and read back the confirmation. You do not argue about the price; if it surprises you, you only ask once whether that is really the longest it can go, and accept the answer. When the agent confirms the domain is renewed and gives you the new expiry date, you thank them and hang up.
